newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen maintaining firm tone vs yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen maintaining firm tone vs yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be firm against the yen in Asia after rising above 118 yen overnight amid lingering bullish sentiment towards the greenback, dealers said.
But possible offers from exporters and life insurers on rises may cap the dollar's advance near 118.50 yen, they said.

"There was talk that a major Japanese life insurer was placing offers near 118.50 yen overnight," a trust bank dealer said, adding that the greenback's rise may be limited around that level. But he added: "If the dollar clearly breaks above that level, it could head towards 119 yen."
Dealer said they would be closely watching the release of Japan's preliminary industrial output data for June and forecasts for July and August due out at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).

Economists' predictions for industrial output ranged from a fall of 1.2 percent to a fall of 4.0 percent for June, compared with the Ministry of International Trade and Industry's (MITI) forecast of a 2.6 percent drop in manufacturers' output.

"If the data shows weak figures, that could be another dollar supportive factor, as it would show the difference in the strength of economic conditions between the two countries (the United States and Japan)," the trust bank trader said.
But a city bank dealer said exporters, including automakers, are likely to sell dollars on the upside.
The dollar ended higher in New York on Tuesday, climbing to a 2-1/2-month high of 118.45 yen against the yen and recouping most of its brief losses against the mark.
Tokyo dealers said the dollar will be top-heavy against the mark near 1.84 marks on profit-taking interest as the rate goes through a downward correction period.
Meanwhile, the mark is seen firm against the yen above 64 yen, but the trust bank dealer said a major Japanese automaker is rumoured to be keen to sell marks near 64.50 yen.
